Manage the pipeline definitions a run executes

## Usage

`circleci pipeline <command> [flags]`

## General Commands

| Command  | Description                             |
| -------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `create` | Create a pipeline definition            |
| `list`   | List pipeline definitions for a project |

## Targeted Commands

| Command | Description                     |
| ------- | ------------------------------- |
| `run`   | Trigger a new run of a pipeline |

## Flags

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Details

Create and list pipeline definitions for a CircleCI project.

A pipeline definition decides what happens when a run is triggered:
which repository to check out and where to find the config YAML that
CircleCI compiles into workflows. Attach triggers to a definition with
'circleci project trigger create', and list the runs one produced with
'circleci run list'.

Inspect, rerun and cancel workflows (job graphs)

## Usage

`circleci workflow <command> [flags]`

## General Commands

| Command | Description                             |
| ------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `list`  | List workflows for a run or recent runs |

## Targeted Commands

| Command  | Description               |
| -------- | ------------------------- |
| `cancel` | Cancel a running workflow |
| `get`    | Get workflow details      |
| `open`   | Open workflow in browser  |
| `rerun`  | Rerun a workflow          |

## Flags

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Details

Work with CircleCI workflows.

Workflows orchestrate jobs within a run. Use these commands to
inspect workflow status, rerun failed jobs, or cancel a running workflow.

Workflow IDs are shown in the output of 'circleci run get'.

Trigger, watch, approve and cancel runs, and list artifacts

## Usage

`circleci run <command> [flags]`

## General Commands

| Command | Description                    |
| ------- | ------------------------------ |
| `list`  | List recent runs for a project |

## Targeted Commands

| Command     | Description                                           |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `approve`   | Approve an approval job that is on hold               |
| `artifacts` | List and download the artifacts of every job in a run |
| `cancel`    | Cancel a run                                          |
| `get`       | Get a run's status                                    |
| `open`      | Open the current project's runs page in the browser   |
| `trigger`   | Trigger a new run of a pipeline                       |
| `watch`     | Watch a run until it completes                        |

## Flags

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Details

Work with CircleCI runs.

A run is one execution of a pipeline, created each time a trigger
fires. It carries the VCS context for that firing and groups the
workflows it produced; each workflow in turn contains jobs.

List recent runs for a project

## Usage

`circleci run list [flags]`

Aliases: `circleci run ls`

## Flags

| Flag                   | Description                                                                       |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-b, --branch string`  | Filter by branch                                                                  |
| `-B, --current-branch` | Filter by the currently checked-out branch                                        |
| `--jq string`          | Process values from the response using jq syntax (see `circleci help formatting`) |
| `--json`               | Output as JSON                                                                    |
| `--limit int`          | Maximum number of runs to show [default: 10] (default 10)                         |
| `--project string`     | Project slug (e.g. gh/org/repo); defaults to git remote                           |
| `--status string`      | filter by run status, e.g. success or failed                                      |

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Examples

- List recent runs for the current project: 
  `circleci run list`
- Filter to the branch you have checked out: 
  `circleci run list --current-branch`
- Filter to a specific branch: 
  `circleci run list --branch main`
- List runs for an explicit project: 
  `circleci run list --project gh/org/repo`
- Show the last successful run: 
  `circleci run list --status success --limit 1`
- Output as JSON for scripting: 
  `circleci run list --json`

## Details

List recent runs for a CircleCI project.

A run is one execution of a pipeline. The project is inferred from the
current git repository's remote unless overridden with --project.

JSON fields: id, phase, outcome, current_outcome, branch, tag, revision, repository_url, commit.subject/url/author_name/author_login, created_at, warnings[].type/message/description/url

List workflows for a run or recent runs

## Usage

`circleci workflow list [<run-id>] [flags]`

Aliases: `circleci workflow ls`

## Arguments

`<run-id>` is optional: a run UUID (as shown by `circleci run list --json`)
or a run number (as shown by `circleci run list`).

When omitted, workflows for recent runs in the current project are listed,
grouped by run.

## Flags

| Flag                  | Description                                                                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-b, --branch string` | Filter by branch (recent-runs mode)                                               |
| `--jq string`         | Process values from the response using jq syntax (see `circleci help formatting`) |
| `--json`              | Output as JSON                                                                    |
| `--limit int`         | Number of recent runs to show (recent-runs mode) (default 10)                     |
| `--project string`    | Project slug (e.g. gh/org/repo); defaults to git remote                           |

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Examples

- List workflows for recent runs in the current project: 
  `circleci workflow list`
- Filter to a specific branch: 
  `circleci workflow list --branch main`
- List workflows by run number: 
  `circleci workflow list 75`
- List workflows by run UUID: 
  `circleci workflow list 9e0c9d52-3b7e-4cd6-b5f7-bfc5e4a07e81`
- Output as JSON: 
  `circleci workflow list --json`

## Details

List workflows for a CircleCI run, or for recent runs in the project when
no run is given.

JSON fields (single run): id, name, phase, outcome, current_outcome.
Recent-runs mode adds run_id.

version: 2.1

functions:
  setup-go: github.com/circleci-functions/setup-go@v0.6.0

commands:
  setup:
    steps:
      - checkout
      - install-go
      - install-task

  # Installs the toolchain and restores the module, build and lint caches, saved at job end.
  install-go:
    steps:
      - setup-go:
          with:
            version-file: go.mod
            golangci-lint-cache: true
            checksum: '{{ checksum "go.sum" }}_{{ checksum "clikit/go.sum" }}_{{ checksum "tools/go.sum" }}'
      - run: go version

  install-task:
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Install go-task
          command: |
            sh -c "$(curl --location https://taskfile.dev/install.sh)" -- -d -b "$HOME/.local/bin"
            echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> "$BASH_ENV"

  # GoReleaser's dockers_v2 pipe shells out to `docker buildx build`, so the
  # builder and the registry login have to exist before it runs.
  setup-docker:
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Register QEMU for cross-architecture builds
          # Dockerfile.alpine RUNs `apk add`, once per platform in the manifest,
          # so building its arm64 half on an amd64 host needs binfmt handlers
          # registered. Idempotent, and a no-op for the cimg/base image, which
          # only COPYs.
          command: docker run --privileged --rm tonistiigi/binfmt --install arm64
      - run:
          name: Create a buildx builder
          # The machine image's default buildx driver is `docker`, which can
          # neither build for two platforms in one invocation nor push a
          # manifest list. A docker-container driver can do both.
          command: docker buildx create --use --driver docker-container
      - run:
          name: Log in to Docker Hub
          # Absent on branch dry-runs, which have no context: the snapshot build
          # still exercises the Dockerfile, it just pushes nothing.
          command: |
            if [ -z "${DOCKER_HUB_USERNAME:-}" ]; then
              echo "No Docker Hub credentials — skipping login (snapshot builds do not push)."
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "$DOCKER_HUB_PASSWORD" | docker login --username "$DOCKER_HUB_USERNAME" --password-stdin

  store_results:
    steps:
      - store_test_results:
          path: ./test-reports

  linux:
    machine:
      image: ubuntu-2604:current
    resource_class: large.gen3

  # Arm64 counterpart to `linux`, for checking both halves of a multi-arch
  # image. Deliberately small: it only pulls and runs a container.
  linux-arm:
    machine:
      image: ubuntu-2604:current
    resource_class: arm.medium

  macos:
    macos:
      xcode: 26.5.0

  windows:
    machine: true
    resource_class: windows.medium

  check:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - run: task ci:check
      - store_results

  test:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - setup
      - run: task ci:test
      - store_results

      # stops cheaply.
      gate_steps:

        default: []
      publish_steps:

        default:
          - run: task ci:release

# arch inside the container makes the log say which half of the manifest ran. A
  # tag missing this platform fails here anyway — the arm machine images carry no
  # binfmt, so there is nothing to silently emulate an amd64-only image with.
  smoke-test-docker:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci/circleci-cli:v1
          command: docker run --rm circleci/circleci-cli:v1 sh -c 'uname -m; circleci version'
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci/circleci-cli:v1-alpine
          command: docker run --rm circleci/circleci-cli:v1-alpine sh -c 'uname -m; circleci version'

  # Opens or updates the release PR (see RELEASE.md).
  release-pr:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - run: task ci:release-pr

  docs:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - run:
          name: Generate reference and build the site
          command: task docs:build
      - run:
          name: Check internal links
          command: task docs:test
      - store_artifacts:
          path: docs/website/public
      - persist_to_workspace:
          root: .
          paths:
            - "docs/website/public"

  docs-publish:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - attach_workspace:
          at: .
      - run:
          name: Publish to gh-pages
          command: task ci:docs:publish

  ok-to-deploy:
    type: no-op

workflows:
  ci:
    jobs:
      # gh-pages holds only generated HTML — never run CI on it. Entry jobs (no
      # `requires`) must opt out explicitly; downstream jobs are gated by these.

      - check:
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - test:
          matrix:
            parameters:
              executor:
                - linux
                - macos
                - windows
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - docs:
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - deploy:
          name: dry-run
          publish_steps:
            - run: task ci:build
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore:
                - main
                - gh-pages

      - ok-to-deploy:
          requires:
            - check
            - test
            - docs
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - release-pr:
          # One at a time, so two pushes can't race to rewrite release/next.
          serial-group: << pipeline.project.slug >>/release-pr
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy
          context:
            - devex-release

      # Publishes only on the push that merges the release PR; halts otherwise.
      - deploy:
          serial-group: << pipeline.project.slug >>/deploy
          gate_steps:
            - run:
                name: Halt unless the release is unpublished
                command: task ci:halt-unless-unreleased
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy
          context:
            - devex-release
            - macos-codesigning

      - docs-publish:
          serial-group: << pipeline.project.slug >>/docs-publish
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy
          context:
            - devex-release

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-snap
          executor: linux
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install snapd
                command: sudo apt update --yes && sudo apt install snapd --yes
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Snap stable channel
                # /snap/bin has to be prepended, not just present: the machine
                # image ships its own circleci in /usr/local/bin, which would
                # otherwise shadow the snap and make this job verify the build
                # agent's CLI instead of the release.
                command: |
                  sudo snap install circleci
                  echo 'export PATH="/snap/bin:$PATH"' >> "$BASH_ENV"
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-brew
          executor: macos
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Homebrew preview tap
                command: |
                  brew update
                  rm -f /opt/homebrew/bin/circleci
                  brew install circleci-public/circleci/circleci@next
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test-docker:
          matrix:
            parameters:
              executor:
                - linux
                - linux-arm
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-choco
          executor: windows
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Chocolatey
                command: choco install circleci-cli -y
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

Inspect a job's details, output and artifacts

## Usage

`circleci job <command> [flags]`

## Targeted Commands

| Command          | Description                            |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `artifact`       | List or download artifacts for a job   |
| `get`            | Get job details                        |
| `open`           | Open job in browser                    |
| `output`         | Work with job step output              |
| `resource-usage` | Work with a job's CPU and memory usage |

## Flags

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Details

Work with CircleCI jobs.

Jobs are the individual units of work within a workflow.

# Changelog

All notable changes to the CircleCI CLI will be documented in this file. Each release's section
is added by its release PR (see [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md)) and becomes its GitHub release notes.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [1.18.0] - 2026-11-19

### What's Changed
* Move run trigger and pipeline run onto the v3 runs API by @gcirclest in https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/pull/2006
* Add test step using testsuite to generated config by @morganmahan in https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/pull/2008
* Say when a failed request may still have taken effect by @EnoshAnwar in https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/pull/2013
* CF2-993: Let extensions shut down cleanly on Ctrl+C / SIGTERM by @joaquin-sm-cci in https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/pull/1983

### New Contributors
* @morganmahan made their first contribution in https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/pull/2008

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/compare/v1.17.0...v1.18.0

## [1.17.0] - 2026-11-18

### What's Changed
* Stop replaying POST and PATCH requests the server may have acted on by @EnoshAnwar in https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/pull/2010


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/compare/v1.16.0...v1.17.0

## [1.16.0] - 2026-11-18

### What's Changed
* Record extension subcommand and exit code on command_invocation by @Fab10-CircleCi in https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/pull/1964
* Check pipeline create's GitHub Actions config path (AEX-133) by @joel-thompson in https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/pull/1979
* Move CLI provider lists into the provider registry (AEX-97) by @joel-thompson in https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/pull/1985
* Accept Forgejo in pipeline create and trigger create (AEX-97) by @joel-thompson in https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/pull/1986
* List an empty job's artifacts as empty instead of not found (AEX-99) by @joel-thompson in https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/pull/1987
* Add run artifacts and run list --status (AEX-99) by @joel-thompson in https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/pull/1988
* Let function commands run without login by @stiyyagura0901 in https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/pull/1996
* Show hostname, IP and last task time on runner instance list by @gcirclest in https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/pull/1995

## What I found

I pulled the CircleCI run history for `gh/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli` and drilled into the `deploy` job of every `main`‑branch run, since that's the job that actually ships the CLI (Homebrew, Snap, Chocolatey, Docker Hub, GitHub release) — see `.circleci/config.yml`'s `ci` workflow, where `deploy` on `main` first runs `task ci:halt-unless-unreleased` and only proceeds to `setup-docker`/`snapcraft`/`choco`/`task ci:release` if there is actually a new, unpublished version ready.

**This week (Nov 23–25, the runs available), no new version was actually deployed to production.**

Every `main`‑branch run this week (triggered by PR merges from alexandrahsu‑eng, Joel Thompson, Ben Crevis, Gabriel Circleci/gcirclest, Shawon Crosen, etc.) ran the `deploy` job, but each one halted within ~6–11 seconds at the `task ci:halt-unless-unreleased` step — confirmed by inspecting the job steps directly (no `setup-docker`, `snapcraft`, `choco`, or `task ci:release` steps ran). That means nothing new was published; the pipeline just confirmed there was no pending release to ship.

In parallel, the automated `release-pr` job has been continuously rebasing a pending release (`release/next` branch, commit subject "Release v1.19.0", authored by the bot `CircleCI Publish` / `cci-publish`), but that PR has **not** been merged into `main` yet, so v1.19.0 has not gone out.

**Most recent actual production deployment:**
- **Version v1.18.0**, published **2026‑11‑19**, via the merge of release PR **#2014** (`release/next` → `main`), merge commit authored by **Enosh Anwar (`EnoshAnwar`)**.
- I verified this by inspecting that run's `deploy` job steps directly: it ran the full publish path — QEMU setup, buildx builder, Docker Hub login, snapcraft/choco install, and `task ci:release` (which took ~6 minutes) — and `CHANGELOG.md` confirms `[1.18.0] - 2026-11-19`, matching the PRs bundled in that release.
- The two releases before that (v1.17.0 and v1.16.0, both 2026‑11‑18) were also merged via `release/next → main`, triggered by **Enosh Anwar** and **Samba siva Tiyyagura (`stiyyagura0901`)** respectively.

**Bottom line:** If "this week" means the last few calendar days (Mon–Wed, Nov 23–25), **no deployment actually reached production** — every `deploy` run halted with nothing new to ship. If you count the trailing 7 days, the only real production deployment was **v1.18.0 on Nov 19, triggered by Enosh Anwar** merging the release PR. There is a v1.19.0 release queued up (bot-maintained on `release/next`) but it hasn't shipped yet.
